learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems in their specialty, which comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability and skill to plan and carry out experimental research, interpret results, and reach conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment, and tools, engineering technology and processes, and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formulation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Selects and dimensions the machinery, tools, implements, and work parameters for various machining processes.

assessment_methods.method: Written and oral individual tests for evaluating technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, delivered documentation, presentation, and technical defense

assessment_rules: For written and oral tests, the recovery mechanism involves retaking written and oral tests. For project-based work, continuous evaluation of the semester project is conducted, with feedback provided a week before the final delivery; corrections applied to the final project version serve as the recovery mechanism. The syllabus does not specify an overall grading formula or minimum marks for the course beyond the component weights for individual learning outcomes.
